title: Jimmy Blanton's inspiration, sound and technique
summary: They discuss Blanton's violin background and cousin Wendell Marshall, and Callender praises his force and big sound.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: From what Jimmy Blanton was playing? Well, I guess my knowledge hadn't reached that point by that time. But after hearing him and becoming friends with him, and I used to hang out with him when the band was in town, and we'd stay up all night... I'd just lug him and my bass around just to hear him play. And I'm sure that was as great an inspiration to me as it was to most bass players?
Who and what was his inspiration? Did he just suddenly conceive of the bass as being an instrument that should and could be played differently than anyone had ever played it before? Or what?
I think he had started on the violin; I'm not sure. I know Wendell Marshall was his cousin. Is Wendell Marshall still alive?
Yes, Wendell is living in St. Louis, but he's not playing any more.
That's a waste. He was a great bass player.
I understand Wendell is a minister, or he's very involved...
...in religion now, and gave up playing music, is what I was told.

Hmm, well. Anyhow, he was a good bass player, too, but not of the same caliber as Blanton. Blanton was very forceful, and what a big sound, and what technique, and what beautiful fingers. He seemed to be able to pick up any instrument and really play it -- any bass, that is. That's something that a lot of us don't do. We have our instruments set up in a way that's comfortable for us, and we do it that way. But I'd have to say that Blanton was a major inspiration to me friendship-wise and playing.
